message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "on: pull_request
name: Pull Request

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          cache: 'npm'
          node-version: 24
      - name: Install dependencies
        env:
          CI: true
        run: npm install
      - name: Test
        run: npm test
      - name: Type-check public types
        run: npm run test:types
      - name: Build library
        run: npm run build:lib
      - name: Test built package
        run: npm run test:dist
      - name: Check docs links
        run: node tools/check-doc-links.mjs
",
  "rationale": "The workflow is a pull_request CI with a single job that already caches npm dependencies via setup-node cache, so P-LIT-GHA-CACHE is contraindicated (equivalent cache exists). There is no matrix (P-LIT-FAIL-FAST not applicable) and ci_history shows no completed runs, so a custom timeout lacks representative history (P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT precondition unmet). P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE fits: runs on the same PR are the same workflow/branch, newer pushes supersede older checks, it is not release/deployment work, and grouping by github.ref keeps distinct PRs isolated. Adding concurrency with cancel-in-progress cancels superseded runs on new pushes while the latest revision still executes the full install/test/typecheck/build/docs suite, preserving coverage.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE"]
}
